name: EMIAC Technologies Limited
summary: EMIAC is a content, reputation-management and digital-marketing services agency, not a demonstrated recurring-revenue software product company. Its real achievement is rapid commercial expansion: comparable revenue rose from ₹2.94 crore in FY2023 to ₹32.31 crore in FY2026. The decisive concern is what shareholders retain after third-party delivery costs, additional staff and software subscriptions: FY2026 operating EBIT fell despite sales growth, and the second half lost money. Concentrated, cancellable client work and a substantial non-operating unquoted investment limit the quality assessment. CAP is not scoreable because sustainable incremental-capital or unit/cohort returns are unproven. Consequently BQS and Growth Quality are null, with missing-evidence bounds of 4.56–5.64 and 5.60–6.95, and are not quality-ranking eligible. IAS is also null because Q and executable-liquidity evidence are incomplete. An annually funded, assumption-dependent five-year base case returns −3.6% annually at ₹83, materially below the 15% hurdle; it is not a promise or a precise fair-value observation. The thesis is a speculative growth/operating-execution situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. Repeatable retained-value growth, renewal evidence and cash returns on the IPO spending would change that view. [S1 PDF pp 79–98; S2 printed pp 30–32,115–116,197–199; E01–E07]
score_note: CAP and L are null. BQS/GQS/IAS remain null and not rankable; original-weight missing-data bounds are shown. IAS also propagates the BQS subcomponent bounds without imputing Q. Display half-up one decimal; no reweighting.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The legal issuer is EMIAC Technologies Limited, formerly EMIAC Technologies Private Limited, incorporated 20 January 2017 and converted to a public company on 10 December 2024. CIN U72200RJ2017PLC056862; ISIN INE1OSW01015; BSE SME scrip 544747, trading name EMIAC. The official interoperability master uses EMIAC$ and an eligible SM row; that is not an NSE listing. BSE listing commenced 13 April 2026. The post-IPO 12,243,149 shares imply ₹101.6181 crore market capitalization at ₹83. The 1,200-share board lot costs ₹99,600. Historical accounts are standalone Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not assumed Ind AS. There were no subsidiaries at March 2026; the subsequently approved US shell is considered separately, with no invented acquired earnings. [S1; S2; S5; S6; E01,E09,E15]

G1 Integrity: Conditional. Related-party business, legal allegations and compliance delays merit monitoring, but the reviewed evidence does not establish issuer diversion, market manipulation or abusive minority treatment. G2 Financial reliability: Conditional. An unmodified audit and working audit trail are favorable; small original/restated differences, a remuneration-payable inconsistency and generic revenue-recognition policy need reconciliation. They are bounded rather than a demonstrated material invalidation of the accounts. G3 Funding: Conditional. Low drawn debt and earmarked IPO resources support restrained operations; October cash and commitments are not verified, and accelerated expansion can consume the buffer. A discretionary, stressed expansion plan is not an actual default. G4 Tradability: Hold — unresolved. Exact lot/shares are verified, but a complete 60-session traded-value history, zero-trade status, executable spread and current BSE surveillance conditions are not. [E08–E15,E24–E27]

Confidence is High in identity and the retrieved audited headline numbers; Medium in comparable historical economics, governance and conditional low-return modeling; Low in sustainable incremental-capital economics, current executable liquidity and a precise present cash balance. Overall investment-action confidence is therefore Low. There is no favorable investment classification. Qualitative comparison remains useful, but CAP lacks the evidence needed for a numerical factor score. BQS and GQS therefore cannot enter numerical quality rankings. This exclusion follows missing CAP evidence, not G3 alone; a funding Hold would not automatically invalidate otherwise supported quality comparisons. All universe rankings remain provisional.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors, each assigned once: GOV 5, MOAT 3, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP null, CASH 5, BAL 6, EXEC 5, EARN 5; IAS factors R 1, D 3, P 4, L null. The machine-readable factor audit supplies at least two material facts, a contrary fact, source-specific evidence and confidence for each. A missing factor is not a neutral 5.

BQS known contribution is 1.00 + 0.60 + 0.96 + 0.50 + 0.50 + 0.48 + 0.40 = 4.44. Coverage is 88%; CAP's original 12% weight gives the mathematical bound 4.56–5.64. GQS known contribution is 3.20 + 1.00 + 0.75 + 0.50 = 5.45. Coverage is 85%; the 15% missing CAP weight gives 5.60–6.95. Both final point scores are null. Neither governance nor persistent value-destruction overrides are triggered. Revenue's ≥30% historical schedule starts at 9 but is capped at 8 for Medium confidence and only four comparable annual observations; no additional small-base penalty or trajectory uplift is applied.

IAS uses Q = final BQS, so Q remains null rather than a midpoint. Direct known contribution is 0.35 × 1 + 0.20 × 3 + 0.10 × 4 = 1.35, direct-factor coverage 65%, and the generic missing-Q/L bound is 1.70–4.85. Propagating the known BQS subcomponents gives the tighter mathematical bound 0.25 × [4.56,5.64] + 1.35 + [0.10,1.00] = 2.59–3.76, with 87% leaf-evidence coverage. These are not statistical confidence intervals or rankable point scores. No missing weight is redistributed. Moving the scored judgments GOV and MOAT together by one point moves both BQS bound endpoints by ±0.40; EARN and CASH together move both GQS endpoints by ±0.25. CAP uncertainty is handled by its full missing-data range, not an arbitrary ±1 around 5. [E03–E28; score_audit]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company sells content creation, branding/online reputation management, digital marketing, and technical/business-automation services. FY2025 service mix was respectively 43.42%, 31.80%, 14.75% and 10.03%. Projects use employees, freelancers, publishing networks and third-party technology. Customers buy delivery outcomes and campaign support; there is no evidence that reported revenue is a contracted SaaS subscription base. The issuer explicitly says it owns no proprietary media inventory and generally operates order by order without long-term customer contracts. Contracts can be changed or cancelled without material penalties. Management reports no cancellation-driven adverse impact in the three historical years, an important contrary fact rather than proof of future retention. [S2 printed pp 30–32,141–161; E02–E05]

FY2025 had 122 clients versus 83 in FY2024 and 94 in FY2023. Repeat clients were 51,44,31 and contributed 45.67%,89.08%,56.26% of revenue. H1FY2026 had 84 clients,55 repeat clients and 73.73% repeat revenue, but a half-year share is not an annual retention rate or ARR. FY2026 exports were ₹6.9380 crore,21.47% of revenue, versus ₹5.7722 crore,29.07% in FY2025. Export growth was approximately 20.2%; domestic growth was much faster. The US presence is a potential sales channel, not existing acquired turnover. FY2026 service-mix disclosure is insufficient to allocate its new ₹5.3095 crore direct-event-execution cost to revenue or a recurring segment. [S1 notes 17,21,26; S2 KPI table; E04,E06,E15]

Revenue is reported gross as service revenue net of discounts, with advertising/marketing and other service delivery expensed. The generic AS revenue policy does not provide a complete principal-versus-agent assessment for every campaign. We retain audited reported revenue and separately calculate an economic retained-value proxy, not an invented accounting gross profit. The proxy subtracts advertising, freelancers, technical service costs, commissions and events, with a second version also deducting professional fees. It avoids treating gross billings growth as software economics. [E02,E06]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Client relationships and execution processes can produce repeat orders: that is the proposed mechanism. The evidence is growing customers and repeat revenue, not protected pricing power or high switching costs. Durability is limited by cancellable work, alternative agencies/freelancers, platform rules and supplier dependence. A capable entrant needs delivery talent, publishing/vendor relationships and acquisition spending, but no scarce licence, exclusive inventory or proprietary platform barrier is established. AI-based production may improve productivity while also commoditizing routine content; no audited unit-cost advantage or defensible proprietary model is demonstrated. Market share with a credible denominator is ND, so no leadership claim is awarded. [S2 pp 30–32, business chapter; E03–E05]

Client concentration increased: top-one/top-five/top-ten shares were 15.17%/53.33%/76.64% in FY2025 and 25.82%/63.42%/79.07% in H1FY2026. Supplier concentration is also material: H1 top-one 46.99%, top-five 86.06%, top-ten 90.01% of the defined direct-expense base. Those denominators are not total company expenses. The largest customer could therefore remove more than the current profit cushion while key vendors still need payment. Management's lack of historical interruptions is favorable, but no long-term or exclusive supplier contracts neutralize the risk. [S2 printed pp 30–32; E03,E05]

Economically relevant comparators are R K SWAMY, Crayons Advertising and Adcounty Media, not a premium SaaS basket. FY2026 group revenue/PAT/CFO were ₹340.7543/22.1059/38.4165 crore for R K SWAMY; ₹313.0478/4.1349/−4.6811 for Crayons, with only ₹3.7672 crore PAT attributable to owners; and ₹86.1090/20.2512/−10.9123 for Adcounty. EMIAC standalone was ₹32.3141/3.6173/3.1040. Crayons and Adcounty show why profit or gross sales alone is inadequate; R K SWAMY provides a larger, diversified integrated-marketing comparator. Different media pass-through, development capitalization, acquisition scopes and minority interests prevent treating these margins or multiples as directly interchangeable. No current peer share-price multiples were independently rebuilt, so none are used as an observed valuation anchor. [S7 consolidated P&L/CF; S8 printed pp 106–108; S9 printed pp 142–143; E18]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Comparable standalone revenue was ₹2.9417,5.3180,19.8562 and 32.3141 crore in FY2023–FY2026. The three-year CAGR is approximately 122.3%, using four observations. Annual additions were ₹2.3763,14.5382 and 12.4579 crore; growth was 80.8%,273.4% and 62.7%. Five- and ten-year comparable CAGRs are ND, not inferred from fewer observations. Original FY2022 revenue of ₹1.949234 crore provides context only: the old scanned statement has a header/CIN transcription inconsistency and is not the IPO-restated basis. It does not supply a five-year CAGR. [S1; S2 printed 197–199; S4; E06,E07]

There is no acquired operating business in the historical reporting perimeter, so the reported growth is constant-entity expansion, but a quantified price/volume/currency bridge is not available. New customers, service mix and domestic demand are evidenced contributors. The external-cost retained-value proxy rose from ₹1.9691 crore in FY2023 to ₹8.6735 in FY2026, roughly 63.9% CAGR. After also deducting professional fees it rose from₹1.7017 to₹7.2470, roughly 62.1% CAGR. That supports genuinely increased activity, though much less than gross sales. In FY2026 the before-professional proxy grew only 13.8%, and the after-professional proxy fell about 1.8%. This current deterioration prevents interpreting 122% historical sales CAGR as a sustainable forward run-rate. [E06,E07]

H1FY2026 revenue/PAT were₹14.1231/4.5477 crore. Full-year less H1 gives H2 revenue₹18.1910 crore but PAT−₹0.9304 crore. This is a derived bridge across the same FY2026 entity, not invented quarterly reporting. Latest FY2027 H1 results and current quarterly CFO were not located as of the cutoff; no fabricated TTM or annualization of H1's 32.2% PAT margin is used. [E07]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
There is accessible demand for content, search visibility, reputation management and automation, and EMIAC has already won more clients. However, the route to scale requires paying writers, publishers, technology vendors, salespeople and managers, not merely activating unused software capacity. The IPO proposes₹1.6789 crore hardware,₹4.0425 crore software/cloud subscriptions,₹5.4150 crore manpower,₹8.80 crore working capital and₹3.90 crore branding. Most software, hiring and branding is recurring economic spending, not an asset that creates free future profit. Planned 97 new hires and references to approximately 125 post-issue staff must be reconciled with 38 employees at 31 January 2026; the headcount dates/descriptions do not form a clean operational roll-forward. [S2 objects pp 93 onward; E16]

The base model grows sales 15% annually to₹65.0 crore while loading first-year staff costs₹7.23 crore and software/cloud₹3.50 crore, including existing costs and remaining expansion allocations. External delivery cost falls to 65% of sales from the FY2026 broad proxy 73.2%, already assuming better mix/productivity. Other overhead is₹2.0 crore initially. Existing client economics provide a bottom-up feasibility cross-check: FY2025₹19.8562 crore across 122 clients was about₹16.28 lakh per client. ₹65 crore needs about 399 equivalent clients at that ticket, or about 313 if average ticket rises 5% annually for five years. Those are equivalents, not disclosed customer forecasts. The company has not yet demonstrated that acquisition pace, retention or sales productivity; a global digital-advertising TAM cannot substitute for it. [E04,E16,E24]

Reported historical capital returns are high on a small net asset base supported partly by customer advances and suppliers, but this is not evidence of sustainable incremental economics. From 31 March 2023 to 31 March 2026, the broad cash/investment-adjusted IC proxy rises from ₹0.1944 crore to ₹2.7944 crore. NOPAT at a consistent illustrative 25% tax rate rises from ₹0.38610 crore to ₹3.36105 crore: arithmetic ΔNOPAT/ΔIC = ₹2.97495/₹2.60 = 114.4%. We retain that arithmetic for audit, but classify the economic incremental-return ratio as NM rather than scoring it. The capital denominator contains net working-capital, tax and deposit movements; cumulative FY2024–FY2026 capex less D&A is only ₹0.1681 crore, compared with ₹2.60 crore IC growth. The approximate ₹2.4319 crore remainder does not identify a matured investment cohort. Expensed customer acquisition, staffing and software costs and changing service mix are not linked to subsequent contract contribution or cash payback. No evidence separates returns on new investment from repricing, mix or utilization of existing operations. A small starting base alone would not invalidate a properly reconciled return, but that reconciliation and attribution are missing here. FY2025-to-FY2026 IC falls, so the one-year incremental ratio is also NM. No customer/service cohort contribution margin, acquisition cost, retention-adjusted lifetime value, payback series or matured IPO-program return supplies the permitted substitute. CAP is therefore null, not 5 and not a punitive low score. The illustrative 13–18% nominal operating-capital opportunity-cost range cannot establish a positive spread without a credible return measure; the separate equity hurdle remains 15%. [S1 PDF pp 79–98; S2 printed pp 197–239; E17; capital_evidence_review.json]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Shivam Bhateja and Divya Gandotra each held 3,059,270 shares before and after the IPO; Dushyant Gandotra is also a promoter. Aggregate promoter/promoter-group ownership falls from about 68% to about 50% after the fresh issue; this is dilution, not an inferred promoter sale. The prospectus discloses no promoter encumbrance at its date. A complete independently verified October pledge/shareholding history is ND. Divya's FY2026 remuneration was₹0.48 crore, versus₹0.28 crore, about 13.3% of FY2026 PAT. Related Macobs Technologies is controlled by KMP/directors: FY2026 services₹1.0547 crore and closing customer advance₹0.4710 crore are disclosed. Gross/GST-inclusive RPT amounts must not be casually compared with net service revenue. [S1 note 24; S2 capital structure/RPT notes; E10]

A separate₹4.25 crore investment in 85,000 Saketh Sevenstar Industries shares at₹500 is recorded under a 1 June 2025 purchase agreement with Quantum Investments. It is a financial investment, not a consolidated operating acquisition; no earnings credit is taken. It is roughly 33.6% of pre-IPO March 2026 book equity, so the investment rationale, relationship checks, investee accounts and exit rights deserve scrutiny. No related-party status or diversion is inferred without evidence. The base terminal recovery is 50%, bear 0%, bull 100%; it is never assumed to fund operations. [S1 note 12; E11]

The FY2026 NAVP & Associates opinion is unmodified; the auditor reports an operating, preserved audit trail and no reported fraud/default in the matters reviewed. This is favorable but not a guarantee. The prospectus discloses historical ROC/GST/TDS and employee-contribution delays. An ESIC demand was paid in June 2025; a 23 September annual-report corrigendum corrected governance/committee/address details and the CSR disclosure, including₹5 lakh spent. These facts support monitoring controls, not labeling the company fraudulent. [S1 audit/corrigendum; S2 risks; E12]

Legal status is differentiated. A₹2,08,576 GST tax/penalty order concerning Facebook Ireland reverse charge is appealed;₹10,429 pre-deposit was paid, management considers its case valid and no provision was recorded. A31 March 2026 income-tax 148A show-cause concerns a₹10 lakh donation deduction to an allegedly problematic political party; response was pending in the 9 April prospectus. That is neither a conviction nor a final₹10 lakh tax demand. A₹2 crore copyright claim against Macobs and named promoters remains a related-entity case, not automatic issuer debt; the disputed material was voluntarily removed and the defendants contest infringement/damages. Latest court/tax resolution was not found. [S1 note 33; S2 printed 266–270; E13]

Promises versus delivery: April IPO objects are evidenced; by 30 June CARE reports₹17.36 crore used and₹14.39 monitored, including only₹0.02 crore manpower but₹3.55 crore branding and₹3.86 crore GCP. That is deployment, not proof of incremental revenue or ROI. US expansion was approved 25 September: secondary reports describe subscription to 10 million shares at$0.00001 each, total$100, in a newly incorporated Delaware entity. Approval, binding subscription documentation, allotment/completion and actual remittance are not all independently verified; no operating earnings acquisition or material acquisition financing is assumed. The model reserves₹0.001 crore and keeps the plan separate. [S3 pp 7–9; S10; E14–E16]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The financial table and full normalization/calculation bridge are embedded in the canonical JSON and verified_inputs.json. Key comparable rows are:

| Period | Revenue | Operating EBITDA | Operating EBIT | Reported PAT | Normalized PAT* | CFO | Cash capex | FCF proxy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2023 restated |2.9417|0.6005|0.5148|0.3876|0.3812|0.3808|0.2146|0.1662|
| FY2024 restated |5.3180|1.1812|1.0570|0.8358|0.7865|0.4318|0.1804|0.2514|
| FY2025 restated |19.8562|5.7283|5.5452|4.2137|4.0632|1.4016|0.2363|1.1653|
| FY2025 annual comparative |19.8562|5.7283|5.5452|4.2291|4.0786|1.4018|0.2364|1.1654|
| FY2026 audited |32.3141|4.7060|4.4814|3.6173|3.2056|3.1040|0.2833|2.8207|

*Normalized PAT excludes all other income at an illustrative 25% marginal tax rate. Operating EBIT = PBT + finance cost − other income. This is a conservative comparable bridge, not a restatement of audited PAT; some other income may recur. The annual report's EBITDA₹5.2549 includes other income₹0.5489, whereas the operating EBITDA above excludes it. No event cost is added back without evidence it is exceptional. The IPO-restated FY2025 PAT₹4.2137 differs from the annual comparative₹4.2291 mainly through tax adjustments; both are retained. Revenue/PBT reconcile. [S1 pp 79–81, notes 17–25; S2 pp 197–199 and restatement bridge; E07,E08]

Using matched FY2024, annual-comparative FY2025 and FY2026 values, cumulative reported CFO/PAT is₹4.9376/₹8.6822=56.9%, not an average of ratios. Classification matters: the reported CFO working-capital lines include non-current bank-deposit changes. Moving the net₹1.2305 crore deposit placement across those three years from CFO to investing raises analytical conversion to 71.0%; also removing the₹0.2866 crore deferred IPO expense from operating classification raises it to 74.3%. These are classification changes, not newly created cash. The original ratio is retained; CASH5 recognizes both the improvement and the still mixed conversion. FY2026 CFO benefited from₹3.0595 crore receivable release and₹2.3347 crore other-liability growth, offset by₹4.7506 crore supplier repayment,₹1.1334 crore other-noncurrent-asset build and₹1.6079 crore tax paid. Cash capex does not explain weak CFO. [E08]

Average receivable days using revenue as a credit-sales proxy improved from 84.1 in FY2025 to 69.6 in FY2026. Closing receivables fell from₹7.6856 to₹4.6351 crore, but balances beyond six months rose to₹0.2536 crore with no doubtful-debt provision. Customer advances₹3.1063 crore support liquidity but create service obligations. Inventory is zero; contract assets are not separately identified. FY2026₹4.25 crore unquoted investment and₹2.026 crore operating security deposits are not unrestricted cash. Drawn debt is₹0.4027 crore; the RBL facility is secured by₹1.20 crore fixed deposits, while ICICI has current-asset/director-property collateral and guarantees. Undrawn facilities are not assumed permanent committed financing. [S1 notes 6–16; E09,E11,E17]

Return ratios need denominator discipline. On average opening/closing equity, FY2024/FY2025/FY2026 ROE is approximately 94.0%/81.6%/33.3%. The broad operating-capital proxy gives very high ROIC of about 377%/218%/105%, illustrating the tiny, advance-funded denominator rather than proving repeatable project returns. FY2026 operating EBIT over average equity plus drawn debt is about 40.5% ROCE, excluding pending escrow-funded anchor capital; it is a pretax funding-basis ratio that includes non-operating assets, not post-tax ROIC. The exact operating-asset reconciliation at March 2026 is PPE ₹0.4406 + operating deposits ₹2.026 + ONWC ₹0.3227 − gratuity ₹0.2345 = ₹2.5548 crore; the broader ₹2.7944 proxy also retains tax assets and accrued interest. New IPO spending must be assessed against the full cash committed, not these legacy ratios. [E17; financial_analytics]

The exact IPO bridge is important. March cash₹14.0157 includes₹9.7255 anchor escrow, leaving₹4.2902 nonanchor cash. April remaining gross inflow is₹31.752−9.7255=₹22.0265, not another₹31.752. The anchor application liability becomes equity, not a cash repayment. March deferred issue expense₹0.2866 has already been paid; future issue budget after March is₹2.8844. June CARE's total used₹17.36 and remaining₹14.39 reconcile to rounded₹31.75; rounded component remaining amounts sum₹14.40, so the model removes₹0.01 from GCP as a conservative rounding reserve. June monitoring shows proceeds, not the company's entire cash balance; reimbursement timing and Jul–Oct movements are not fabricated. [E09,E14]

The claims register settles every opening debt, employee, statutory, supplier, customer, provision and other claim once. Opening ONWC₹0.3227 includes legacy GST/TDS/EPF/ESIC and customer advances. Debt is outside ONWC and repaid once. Current gratuity ₹0.0308 is paid in year 1; long gratuity ₹0.2037 and a conservative ₹0.0294 remuneration discrepancy reserve are terminal senior claims. Operating deposits are in the operating enterprise value; income-tax refund, accrued interest and DTA receive no free-cash credit. Restricted IPO cash only reimburses its modeled authorized spending. Remaining restricted cash is not distributed at terminal. No dividend is counted while retaining the same cash. [claims_register; E09,E24]

Current shares include the 3.24 million fresh IPO shares exactly once. Historical FY2026 diluted EPS₹4.02 uses 9.003149 million weighted shares; the same PAT on current shares is about₹2.955, and normalized EPS about₹2.618. Bonus shares are not economic dilution; the fresh issue is. No disclosed options/warrants are added without terms, and no future rescue issue is assumed. [S1 note 25; S2 capital structure; E09]


Capital has been retained rather than returned: the prospectus reports no dividends for FY2023–FY2025, and the FY2026 board recommended none to preserve funds for expansion. No buyback is evidenced in the reviewed history. The forecast likewise pays no dividend, so all retained cash appears only once in terminal equity. [S2 printed 190; S1 directors report, Dividend]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The main method is a five-year operating cash/funding model followed by a terminal operating-EBIT multiple and an explicit enterprise-to-common-equity bridge. A reported/normalized earnings multiple is the cross-check, not the model itself. ₹83 implies 28.1× FY2026 PAT on current shares or 31.7× normalized PAT. An exact current EV multiple is not asserted because October freely available cash and restrictions are not verified; subtracting the entire IPO balance would overstate cheapness. [E24–E26]

The synthetic forward years are October 2026–October 2031, not FY2027 accounting forecasts. Annual closing cash is a timing approximation, not proof of intra-year solvency: monthly collections, payroll, restricted-account release dates and tax payments may create a temporary need even when each modeled year closes positive. A current monthly cash bridge is required before an implementation conclusion. The remaining June resource/use pools are modeled together, with no main-case credit for uncertain legacy free cash or already deployed working capital. All forecast staff/software costs are expensed; authorized IPO releases fund those same costs, not a second deduction. Cash taxes are 25% of positive EBIT, with no immediate loss refund. Debt is repaid in year 1; there are no dividends, new borrowing, share issues or assumed asset-sale rescues. Base growth 15%, external cost 65%,75-day receivables and 30-day supplier credit produce terminal revenue₹65.00 crore, EBIT₹5.53 crore and free cash₹15.14 crore. At 12× EBIT, plus half recovery of the unquoted investment and₹1.2305 crore terminal FD, less senior claims, terminal equity is₹84.68 crore: −3.6% annualized. [model.py; E24]

Bear case loses 20% of sales initially, then grows 3%; direct costs 72%,95-day receivables and reduced discretionary hiring/software spending leave the business funded but near breakeven. Terminal equity₹8.73 crore implies−38.8% annually and about 91.4% capital loss. No positive value is assigned to loss-making terminal EBIT; that is an impairment scenario, not a company liquidation forecast. Bull case requires 30% annual sales growth,60% external costs,60-day collections and 15× EBIT, with more capacity spending. Revenue reaches₹119.98 crore, EBIT₹29.42 crore and equity₹506.81 crore:37.9% annualized. That is a demanding execution case, not the base forecast. [E24]

Reverse valuation under the base cost structure and 12× terminal EBIT requires approximately 22.8% annual revenue growth for five years to earn 15% at₹83, ending around₹90.30 crore revenue and₹14.39 crore EBIT. This is possible relative to past percentage growth, but requires sustained retained-value growth and much better absorption of the new cost base than FY2026 currently shows. A disclosed 5×3 growth/multiple sensitivity varies growth 10–30% and terminal EBIT multiples 8/12/16. Under the base outcome, hurdle-entry prices are approximately₹39.25 at 12%,₹34.39 at 15%, and₹30.23 at 18%; these are assumption-dependent research prices, not observable fair values or automatic buy levels. The full output computes exact values. [E25]

Opening cash₹0–4.2902 and recoverable already-funded WC₹0–5.69 are varied separately: even the most favorable combination leaves base IRR around−1.4%, not 15%. A5% entry and exit-friction sensitivity further reduces return. Thus R1 is robust to these bounded opening-state gaps; it is not left null merely because G3/current cash is conditional. A meaningful change to the recurring cost plan, margin structure or growth evidence would require remodelling rather than an arbitrary factor haircut. [E26]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument to this cautious view is that sales have repeatedly exceeded expectations, client relationships may deepen, IPO spending could reduce outsourced costs, and the core business can operate with much less expansion spending than the full plan. Cash/deposit reclassification also shows better operating conversion than the unadjusted headline ratio. Those positives are explicit in the bull and restrained-survival cases. They do not establish software-like margins or perpetual renewal revenue. [E04,E08,E24]

The linked failure path is a key-client budget cut, lower gross profit, sticky staff/software costs, slower collection, supplier-payment pressure and then a need to cancel growth plans or recapitalize. A separate severe-expansion stress combines 35% sales loss,150-day collections,15-day supplier credit and retaining the aggressive hiring/software path. It develops a first-year deficit around₹2.81 crore and a five-year cumulative gap₹40.63 crore. Its ordinary equity IRR is null: no unfunded positive return or invented rescue financing is shown. Because those expansion costs are not all proven binding and a restrained essential-operation case remains funded, this stress does not by itself make G3 Fail. The restrained case excludes new hiring, reduces discretionary software, retains customer-loss stress and leaves the unspent restricted IPO pools unavailable for equity distribution. [E24,E27]

Permanent impairment risk is High at₹83: even funded survival may earn little relative to market value. The single most important thesis variable is retained operating value after outsourced delivery and the recurring expansion cost base, not headline billing growth. Evidence of persistent cash losses after rightsizing, unrecoverable material receivables, undisclosed encumbrances or an adverse governance finding could invalidate the thesis; an isolated quotation decline would not. [E06,E24,E27]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold price returns in five years require 38.0% and 58.5% annual growth respectively. The bull model comes close to 5× terminal equity with 30% revenue CAGR, materially better direct margins and 15× EBIT; reducing the terminal multiple weakens the result. Tenfold requires a substantially larger and more profitable business or a less defensible valuation premium, while funding added staff and working capital without diluting shareholders. No independent market-share, contracted backlog or mature unit-economics evidence supports tenfold as a base expectation. Fivefold is possible but demanding; tenfold is speculative/unsupported. Neither is inferred from the small starting market capitalization. [E24–E26]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Retained-value growth: FY2026 before-professional proxy₹8.6735 crore and after-professional₹7.2470. Investigate another period of sales growth without retained-value growth; persistent decline after scaling costs is thesis-breaking.
2. Operating margin: FY2026 EBIT13.9% versus 27.9% in FY2025; H2 loss. Require positive comparable-period operating recovery, not a non-operating-income-led PAT rebound.
3. Customer risk: H1FY2026 top-one 25.82%, top-ten 79.07%; no long-term contracts. Review the next disclosed cohort/customer table; losing a material account without replacement and collection is a major warning.
4. Collections: FY2026 average AR69.6 days;₹0.2536 crore older than six months. Investigate a return toward the FY2025 closing-debtor burden, ageing without provision or uncollected related-party balances.
5. IPO deployment: June₹14.39 crore remaining; manpower₹0.02 spent versus branding₹3.55 and GCP₹3.86. Reconcile the next monitor to bank cash, expense/capex classification, authorized use and incremental operating outcomes.
6. Recurring capacity cost: proposed 97 hires, software/cloud₹4.0425 crore. Require actual headcount, payroll, subscription periods and revenue per delivery employee. Unfunded fixed commitments materially change G3.
7. Capital allocation: Saketh investment₹4.25 crore. Seek investee financials, ownership, related-party checks, valuation and exit rights; undisclosed guarantees or value transfers would change governance.
8. Controls/legal matters: obtain GST appeal and donation-inquiry updates, corrected CSR/committee disclosures, and explain the₹2.94 lakh remuneration inconsistency. Allegations are not guilt, but evidence of concealment would be significant.
9. US entity: verify allotment, remittance, ownership and any new commitments. Do not credit acquisition earnings before audited contribution exists.
10. Trading: obtain a complete 60-session BSE traded-value/zero-trade series, current lot, surveillance notices and bid/ask depth before implementation. No automated monitor or trade is created by this plan. [E03–E28]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved implementation and capital-return evidence; speculative growth watchlist, not investment-eligible on the present record. BQS and GQS are null and excluded from numerical quality rankings because CAP lacks sufficient evidence. Their missing-data bounds are 4.56–5.64 and 5.60–6.95. IAS is null; propagating BQS uncertainty plus missing L yields 2.59–3.76, tighter than the generic direct-factor bound of 1.70–4.85. No bound endpoint is a point rating. The low modeled return and material impairment risk are independently supported; this is not a mechanical rejection based on P/E or SME status. GOV 5 does not trigger an Avoid — governance override, and conditional funding is not a demonstrated default. Missing CAP is not proof of persistent value destruction and does not trigger the CAP≤3 GQS cap. [E17,E24–E28]

Research priority is obtaining the post-IPO operating/cash bridge, actual costs, customer recurrence and complete trading evidence. A lower price alone does not repair concentration or missing liquidity. Conversely, demonstrated retained-value growth and disciplined recurring spending could improve the model even without a price fall. No portfolio sizing or sell instruction is inferred because holdings, taxes and executable depth were not supplied. Publication is outside this analysis's authorization.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources are archived locally with hashes and working URLs in source_ledger.json: corrected FY2026 annual report[S1], final 9 April 2026 prospectus[S2], CARE June 2026 monitor[S3], original FY2023 report[S4], official 19 October interoperability master[S5], and three FY2026 peer annual reports[S7–S9]. The₹83 quote and incomplete OHLCV history[S6] are secondary, corroborated by a dated 19 October bulk-deal page. US approval[S10] is secondary because actual completion/remittance documents were not independently retrieved. Primary-source locators sit beside the claims and in evidence_ledger.json; a title-only source list is not being used as proof.

Assumptions are explicitly separated from disclosure. Model growth, margins, cash-cycle days, tax, maintenance capex, terminal multiples, unquoted-investment recovery and future wage/software renewal costs are analyst scenarios. They are not management guidance. The model's main conservative opening state does not assert that June cash is unchanged in October: resources and matching uses move together, and possible core cash/WC recovery is shown separately. No unspecified financing is treated as received.

Open questions that matter most are: current cash/monitored-proceeds reconciliation; gross-versus-net/principal-agent policy for media placements; FY2026 event revenue and costs; actual post-IPO headcount/software commitments; current client concentration, renewals and receivable collections; unquoted investee value/relationships; current promoter encumbrance; US allotment/remittance; litigation status; and complete exchange turnover/current restrictions. Five- and ten-year comparable financial history, reliable market share, contract-level margins, matured incremental-investment returns and peer current valuation multiples remain ND. Sources retrieved 21 October are used only for documents/observations available by 20 October; later facts are excluded. The accompanying Python model, exact Decimal score audit, claims register and nonmutating QA make the calculations reproducible. No previous review or published file is changed.

GOV.reason: Mixed stewardship: clean audit and disclosed controls coexist with compliance delays, RPT exposure and a large unquoted investment.
supporting_facts: The FY2026 audit is unmodified and the audit trail operated.
The ₹4.25 crore financial investment equals 33.6% of March pre-IPO equity.
GOV.contrary_fact: No established issuer diversion or conviction was located.

MOAT.reason: Relationship-led agency with limited demonstrated switching cost or proprietary protection.
supporting_facts: No owned proprietary media inventory or exclusive vendor contracts are disclosed.
Top-ten customers supplied 79.07% of H1FY2026 revenue.
MOAT.contrary_fact: Repeat business and no historical supply interruption support useful relationships.

REV.reason: Comparable3-year expansion and retained-value cross-check justify strong historical growth;history/confidence cap8.
supporting_facts: Comparable revenue grew at 122.3% CAGR over three years.
The retained-value proxy grew at more than 60% CAGR over the same period.
REV.contrary_fact: FY2026 retained value after professional fees declined despite sales growth; no trajectory uplift is awarded.

DUR.reason: Accessible demand and client additions, but variable budgets and weak contractual recurrence.
supporting_facts: The company served 122 clients in FY2025.
IPO proceeds fund staff, software and working-capital capacity.
DUR.contrary_fact: Order-to-order work and concentrated customers constrain visibility.

CAP.reason: Sustainable incremental returns are not established. The aggregate accounting quotient is materially distorted and no evidenced unit/cohort substitute is available.
supporting_facts: FY2023–FY2026 NOPAT increases ₹2.97495 crore on a broad IC increase of ₹2.60 crore, but the accounting quotient cannot attribute profit to matured new investment.
FY2025–FY2026 operating IC falls; no contract/client cohort margin, acquisition-cost/payback series or seasoned IPO investment return was found.
CAP.contrary_fact: Positive core profit and low tangible-capital intensity are favorable, but are not evidence of the return on additional capital.

CASH.reason: Mixed conversion improves materially after justified FD classification, without becoming cycle-proven.
supporting_facts: Reported three-year conversion is 56.9%, improving to 71.0% after fixed-deposit reclassification.
Receivables improved, but customer advances support CFO and aged balances increased.
CASH.contrary_fact: FY2026 CFO is positive at ₹3.104 crore and suppliers were paid down, not stretched.

BAL.reason: Manageable disclosed debt and earmarked resources support restrained operations but not unconstrained expansion.
supporting_facts: Drawn debt was ₹0.4027 crore versus ₹14.39 crore June monitored IPO proceeds.
The restrained stress case is funded without a rescue.
BAL.contrary_fact: IPO cash is earmarked and October balances are unknown; aggressive expansion can exhaust funding.

EXEC.reason: Commercial scale is proven; repeatable post-IPO returns are not yet demonstrated.
supporting_facts: FY2026 revenue grew 62.7%.
CARE documents actual deployment rather than assumed unreceived financing.
EXEC.contrary_fact: The H2 loss and substantial branding/GCP spending precede delivery of most planned hiring.

EARN.reason: Operating business remains profitable, but margin and per-share outcomes deteriorated.
supporting_facts: FY2026 operating EBIT was ₹4.4814 crore versus ₹5.5452 crore previously.
FY2026 PAT of ₹3.6173 crore equals ₹2.955 per current share after the IPO.
EARN.contrary_fact: Normalization does not eliminate profit; most PAT is not an asset-sale gain.

R.reason: Supported conditional base return is more than10percentagepoints below15% hurdle.
supporting_facts: The funded base IRR is −3.58%.
The favorable opening-state sensitivity yields −1.41%, still below the hurdle.
R.contrary_fact: The bull case produces 37.9% under demanding growth and margin conditions.

D.reason: Survival can be funded while equity suffers severe valuation impairment.
supporting_facts: Bear terminal equity is ₹8.73 crore versus ₹101.62 crore entry value.
Severe expansion stress requires external funding and has a null ordinary IRR.
D.contrary_fact: Restrained essential operations remain funded without new debt or equity.

P.reason: Several execution improvements must persist to earn the hurdle.
supporting_facts: The hurdle requires 22.82% five-year revenue growth under base costs and a 12× EBIT exit.
The base outcome supports a ₹34.39 entry at the 15% hurdle, versus ₹83 observed.
P.contrary_fact: Historical growth was higher; the observed price does not require the entire bull outcome.

L.reason: Incomplete market-day/turnover and execution evidence prevents a valid liquidity score.
supporting_facts: The 1,200-share lot is verified.
Observed-only median volume of 8,400 shares permits no whole lot at 5% participation.
L.contrary_fact: The dated 19 October volume of 216,000 shows activity; missing dates are not verified zero-trade sessions.

BQS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-evidence bound, not statistical confidence interval

GQS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-evidence bound, not statistical confidence interval

IAS.bound_type: Mathematical missing-evidence bound, not statistical confidence interval

propagated_bounds.explanation: Direct IAS coverage is 65% because Q and L are null. Known BQS subcomponents permit an 87%-covered leaf-level bound without imputing Q. Both are mathematical missing-evidence bounds, not confidence intervals.

confidence.quality_factors: mixed: scored factors medium; CAP low

ranking_eligibility.reason: CAP is missing, so neither BQS nor GQS has a rankable point score. IAS also lacks L and has G4 hold. The funding gate alone is not the reason quality ranking is excluded.

G1.reason: RPTs, unquoted allocation and compliance/legal matters require monitoring; no substantiated issuer diversion or severe minority abuse.

G2.reason: Unmodified audit; bounded restatement/remuneration differences and gross/net disclosure gap do not materially invalidate quality comparisons.

G3.reason: Restrained essential operations funded; October balances/commitments not verified. Optional severe expansion stress is not an evidenced actual default.

G4.reason: Complete 60-session actual turnover/zero-trade evidence and current executable restrictions/spreads not verified.

valuation.horizon: Five synthetic annual periods from October 2026 to October 2031, not reported fiscal-year forecasts
limitations: This conditional model does not assert a verified October cash balance. June remaining earmarked funds are paired with matching remaining uses; already spent 17.36 is not new cash. Unmatched later losses would reduce funding.

No main-case credit for March nonanchor cash or already deployed 5.69 working capital. Separate opening-state sensitivities show possible recoverable value. These conservative bounds are not a current balance sheet.

IPO wage/software spending is recurring economic expense, not capitalized free growth. Releases pay the same modeled costs once. Plans are not assumed legally committed; restrained survival excludes discretionary expansion.

Opening operating/statutory/customer claims are embedded once in ONWC. Debt is separately paid; current gratuity is paid in year 1 and long gratuity plus a bounded remuneration discrepancy are senior terminal claims. US subscription is a .001 budget, not evidence of remittance.
Annual timing does not prove intra-year liquidity. No future loan, share raise, pledged-deposit release or unquoted-asset sale rescues cash shortfalls. Unfunded ordinary IRRs are null.
Residual restricted IPO cash is excluded from distributable terminal equity. No dividends, NCI or further parent dilution assumed; existing IPO shares included once.
